mentions.name: Arbiter
mentions.description: A tool that AI agents can use to construct structured, validated project specifications, which compile into services with stubbed endpoints, UIs with placeholder components, Dockerfiles/Terraform/K8s infra, E2E tests from declared flows, and GitHub/GitLab epics/issues/subissues. Includes GitHub/GitLab webhook integration so agents can be triggered reactively when events occur on a repo, Cloudflare tunnel support for setting up webhooks in a local dev environment, and a fully customizable project generator.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm trying to get my agentic software specification tool Arbiter to release (UI polish/debugging is so slow :/, browser shenanigans are harder than Rust fr).  It's basically a tool that AI agents can use to construct a project specification. The twist to Arbiter is that the specs are structured and validated, and you can compile them to get:

Services with stubbed endpoints,
UIs with placeholder components,
Dockerfiles/Terraform/K8s infra,
E2E tests (via declared flows),
Github/Gitlab epics/issues/subissues
